evidence.command: getent passwd clusterops; awk -F: '$3 >= 1000 && $1 != "nobody" {print $1 ":" $3 ":" $6}' /etc/passwd; sudo -n find /home/clusterops/.ssh /root/.ssh /etc/ssh -maxdepth 2 -type f -printf '%m %u:%g %p\n' 2>/dev/null; sudo -n -u clusterops -H awk 'NF { for (i=1;i<=NF;i++) if ($i ~ /^(ssh-|ecdsa-|sk-)/) { print "line=" NR " keytype=" $i " option_prefix=" substr($0,1,index($0,$i)-1); n++; break } } END { print "key_entries=" n+0 }' /home/clusterops/.ssh/authorized_keys; sudo -n /usr/sbin/sshd -T; systemctl is-enabled ssh.socket; systemctl is-active ssh.socket; getent ahostsv4 node1 node2 node3; awk '$1 !~ /^#/ && NF >= 2 { for (i=2;i<=NF;i++) if ($i == "node1" || $i == "node2" || $i == "node3") print $i " " $1 }' /etc/hosts; sudo -n ufw status verbose; sudo -n ss -lntup 2>&1
evidence.observation: Only clusterops was listed as a non-system account; exactly two peer-restricted authorized-key entries were present; effective SSH settings used the expected identity, known_hosts, BatchMode, and strict checking; password and keyboard-interactive authentication were disabled; stable mappings were unique; UFW was inactive with no additional rules; listeners were SSH and local platform services only; no candidate backup/temp/debug artifacts were found.
